quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are thinking of renting a flat and want more details before booking a viewing. Lay out the email to the letting agent.
options:
Kind regards,
Sanjana Rao
I saw the listing for Flat 2 on Mill Lane and am interested in viewing it. Could you tell me whether bills are included in the rent and when the flat is available?
Subject: Flat 2, 14 Mill Lane: further details
Dear Mr Hargreaves,
quests.hint: Bring the listing you saw and the exact questions together, so the agent can answer in one reply.
quests.explanation: Naming the property in the subject lets the agent find the listing. Two clear questions about bills and dates are easier to answer than 'please send more information'.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Subject: Difficulty of the Ridge Trail / Greeting: Dear Visitor Centre, / Arrange the rest of this email from someone planning a walk with a young child.
options: I am planning to walk the Ridge Trail with my six-year-old daughter next weekend.
Any advice about parking would also be very welcome.
Is the path suitable for young children, and are there any steep or exposed sections?

Yours faithfully,
Roisin Gallagher
quests.hint: Give the reader the circumstances first, because they change the answer.
quests.explanation: The visitor centre cannot say if a trail is suitable without knowing who will walk it. Giving the child's age first turns a general question into one they can answer confidently.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are a foreign student who needs to know which documents to bring for your visa interview. Subject: Documents needed for visa interview / Greeting: Dear Sir or Madam, / Arrange the body and sign-off.
options: I would also like to know whether photocopies are acceptable.
I have an interview at your consulate on Tuesday, 15 April, for a student visa.

Yours faithfully,
Duc Nguyen
Could you please send me a full list of the documents I need to bring?
quests.hint: Appointment first, main request second, smaller detail last.
quests.explanation: The consulate's staff need the appointment date to see which procedure applies. The list is the main request, so it comes before the smaller question about photocopies.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You want to book a check-up for your dog. Structure the email to the vet.
options: Dear Dr Ferreira,
I would like to book Milo's annual check-up and vaccinations. Mornings are best for me, ideally before the end of the month.
Subject: Appointment request for Milo, annual check-up

Kind regards,
Sophie Dupont
quests.hint: State the purpose of the visit and your availability, so the clinic can suggest a time.
quests.explanation: Clinics can respond faster when you name both the reason for the appointment and when you're free. 'Mornings' and 'before the end of the month' gives them a search window without you fixing an exact time.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Subject: Booking the meeting room for Thursday / Greeting: Hi Facilities Team, / Arrange the body and sign-off.
options: We will be hosting a client presentation for about eight people.
Please let me know if the room is free, and whether you can set up the projector.

Thanks,
Patricia Lund
Could I book Meeting Room B on Thursday, 22 May, from 2 to 4 pm?
quests.hint: Request first, then the reason that explains the size or equipment, and finally the confirmation you need.
quests.explanation: The booking details are the core of the message. The purpose (client presentation for eight) helps the team choose the right room, and the last sentence tells them what confirmation you expect.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You'd like to visit a university before applying. Subject: Request for a campus tour / Greeting: Dear Admissions Office, / Arrange the body and sign-off.
options: I am considering applying for the Architecture degree next year.

Yours faithfully,
Adebayo Ogunleye
I will be in Edinburgh from 3 to 5 August and would like to join a campus tour if one is available.
Could you let me know how to book a place?
quests.hint: Your interest, your dates, then the request for how to proceed.
quests.explanation: The office needs your degree interest so that they can offer the right tour, and your dates so they can check availability. Asking how to book gives them a clear reply to write.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You bought a jacket that doesn't fit and want to return it. Arrange the email.
options: Dear Returns Team,
Subject: Return request for order 30918
I bought a navy jacket (size M) on 2 April, but it is too small. Could you tell me how to return it for a refund?

Kind regards,
Emily Okafor
quests.hint: Include the order number, what is wrong and what outcome you want.
quests.explanation: Returns staff need three things: which order, why it is being returned, and whether you want a refund or exchange. Giving all of them in the first message avoids extra emails.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Your headphones stopped working eight months into a one-year warranty. Subject: Faulty headphones under warranty / Greeting: Dear Support Team, / Arrange the body and sign-off.
options: The left earpiece stopped working last week, even after charging and resetting.

Yours faithfully,
Dominic Reyes
Could you tell me how to arrange a repair or replacement?
I bought a pair of Aura X headphones in September, and they are still under warranty.
quests.hint: Establish that you're entitled to help, then describe the fault and what you tried.
quests.explanation: Noting the warranty first shows why you have a right to support. Mentioning the steps you tried prevents the standard reply 'have you tried turning it off and on?'.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You'd like to exchange a gift for another colour, but you have no receipt. Subject: Exchange without a receipt / Greeting: Dear Manager, / Arrange the body and sign-off.
options: Unfortunately the giver did not include a receipt, but I still have the tags and the original packaging.

Kind regards,
Fatima Sheikh
I received a scarf from your shop as a birthday gift, and I would like to exchange it for a different colour.
Would it be possible to arrange an exchange, or should I ask for a gift receipt?
quests.hint: State the request, explain the obstacle honestly, and offer what you do have.
quests.explanation: The obstacle (no receipt) is stated openly, immediately followed by evidence that the item is unused. Ending with an alternative question keeps the shop able to help in either way.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A parcel you were expecting on Monday still hasn't arrived. Set out the email.
options: My parcel was due on Monday, but it has not arrived, and the tracking page has not changed since Friday. Could you tell me where it is?
Subject: Missing parcel, order 55620, due Monday
Dear Customer Service,

Kind regards,
Harriet Cole
quests.hint: Give the order, what was promised, what you have seen, and what you want to know.
quests.explanation: The order number helps them locate it, the promised date sets the standard, and mentioning the tracking page shows you have already checked. The final question directs their reply.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You need your delivery to go to your office instead. Subject: Change of delivery address for order 71204 / Greeting: Dear Sir or Madam, / Arrange the body and sign-off.
options:
Yours faithfully,
Laszlo Nagy
I will not be at home this week, and the office reception can accept parcels.
Could you confirm by email that the change has been made before it is dispatched?
Please change the delivery address for order 71204 to 22 Harbour Street, Bristol, BS1 4RT.
quests.hint: The change requested must be impossible to miss; then reasons; then the confirmation you require.
quests.explanation: In address changes, the new address must be unmistakable, so it goes in the first sentence. The reason is secondary, and the confirmation request protects against a parcel going to the old address.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You want your neighbour Ms Perera to accept a parcel while you are at work. Subject: Parcel on Wednesday? / Greeting: Hi Ms Perera, / Arrange the message.
options:
Many thanks,
George
I hope you're well.
Would you be able to take it in for me? I'd be happy to pick it up as soon as I get back.
I'm expecting a parcel on Wednesday, but I won't be home until 6 pm.
quests.hint: A neighbourly favour begins gently, then explains the situation, then asks.
quests.explanation: When you ask a neighbour for a favour, the polite greeting first makes the request feel less abrupt. The short explanation shows the need, and the ask is phrased as a question, not an instruction.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You left your wallet on the 8:10 train from Leeds. Put together the email to the train company.
options: Subject: Lost wallet on the 8:10 Leeds to Sheffield train

Yours faithfully,
Priya Menon
I believe I left a brown leather wallet on the 8:10 train from Leeds to Sheffield on Tuesday. It contains a bank card and a student ID in the name of Priya Menon.
Dear Lost Property Team,
quests.hint: Give identifying details that only the owner would know, but not details that would be unsafe to share.
quests.explanation: A description of the item and where it was lost helps staff search. Naming the ID card gives proof of ownership. Notice that you do not need to list card numbers or passwords.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You found a phone in a café and want to contact the owner through the lock screen email. Subject: I found your phone / Greeting: Hello, / Arrange the message.
options:
Best wishes,
Jorge
You can collect it any day before 6 pm, and please bring some ID.
I found a phone with this email address on its lock screen in Café Verde this afternoon.
I gave it to the manager, who will keep it safely behind the counter.
quests.hint: Explain what you found, where it is now, and what the owner must do.
quests.explanation: A message from a stranger should reassure quickly. Saying where the phone is and how to collect it, without asking for anything, lets the owner act immediately.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Your suitcase hasn't arrived after a flight. Subject: Delayed luggage, flight LH902, bag tag 4417 / Greeting: Dear Baggage Services, / Arrange the body and sign-off.
options: My suitcase did not arrive at Frankfurt airport on 12 October.
Please tell me where it is and deliver it to Hotel Rheinblick as soon as it is found.

Yours faithfully,
Aisha Karim
It is a large green case with a red ribbon on the handle, and my tag number is 4417.
quests.hint: First the problem, then how to identify the item, and finally where you need it.
quests.explanation: Baggage staff look for the tag number first, which is why it is in the subject. They then need a physical description, and finally the address where to send the bag.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You have a hospital appointment and need to leave school at lunchtime on Friday. Subject: Permission to leave early on Friday / Greeting: Dear Mr Olsen, / Arrange the body and sign-off.
options: She has an orthodontist appointment at 1:15 pm.
I am writing to ask permission for Freya to leave school at 12:30 on Friday.

Yours sincerely,
Claire Bergman
I will collect her from the school office and provide a note tomorrow.
quests.hint: The request, then its reason, then how it will be handled.
quests.explanation: Asking for permission works best when you make the request obvious and show how you will minimise disruption. Offering to collect her in person answers the school's most likely concern.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You'd like to work from home next Friday. Subject: Working from home on 13 June / Greeting: Hi Natasha, / Arrange the body and sign-off.
options: I'll be online for all my meetings and will finish the report by the end of the day.
I have a boiler engineer coming between 9 and 12, and I can't move the appointment.
Would it be all right if I worked from home next Friday, 13 June?

Thanks,
Carlos
quests.hint: The question, the reason, and reassurance about productivity.
quests.explanation: Managers grant permission more easily when the reason is specific and their main worry (work getting done) is addressed. This is why the last sentence lists what you will do.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You want to record a lecture because you have a hearing difficulty. Subject: Request to record lectures / Greeting: Dear Professor Bell, / Arrange the body and sign-off.
options: I have a hearing difficulty, and I would find it very helpful to record your lectures.
I am a second-year student in your Economics module.
The recordings would be for my own revision only, and I would delete them after the exam.

Kind regards,
Michael Adeyemi
quests.hint: Introduce yourself, give the request and reason, then reassure the professor about use.
quests.explanation: Personal reasons are shared only as far as needed. The final sentence tackles copyright and privacy concerns before the professor needs to raise them.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are choosing between two subjects for next year and want your former teacher's advice. Arrange the email.
options: Subject: Advice on choosing my subjects
Dear Mrs Dlamini,

Best wishes,
Thabo
I am trying to decide between Geography and Computer Science for next year. As you know me well, I would really value your advice.
quests.hint: State the choice, then say why you're asking this particular person.
quests.explanation: Advice requests work when you explain the decision clearly and why the reader is well placed to help. Flattery is not needed; simple honesty about their knowledge of you is enough.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Subject: Learning the new invoicing software / Greeting: Hi Paolo, / Arrange the body of the message from a colleague.
options: Do you have any tips, or could you show me for ten minutes?

Thanks in advance,
Deborah
I'm finding it hard to create recurring invoices.
I noticed you already use the new invoicing software.
quests.hint: Notice, problem, request for help.
quests.explanation: Explaining why you're asking him (he already uses it) makes the request natural. Offering a specific amount of time (ten minutes) makes it easier to agree.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You're thinking of buying a used car from a private seller. Subject: Advice on buying a second-hand car / Greeting: Hi Uncle Femi, / Arrange the message to a relative who knows about cars.
options: I'm thinking of buying a used Honda Fit that has 60,000 miles and costs £6,500.

Thank you,
Bisi
Would you be willing to come and look at it with me, or tell me what to check?
I'd feel much more confident with your help.
quests.hint: Give specifics, ask for the help, and finish with why it matters to you.
quests.explanation: Specifics allow the uncle to judge whether the deal sounds reasonable. Giving him two ways to help (attend or advise) means he can say yes to one even if he is busy.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You're organising a car share to a tournament and need to know who's driving. Subject: Lifts to Saturday's tournament / Greeting: Hi everyone, / Arrange the body and sign-off.
options:
Thanks,
Ben
I can take three people, but we need two more cars.
Please reply by Thursday to say whether you can drive or need a lift.
We need to leave the school at 7:30 am on Saturday to arrive by 9.
quests.hint: The group needs the timing, the shortage and the response deadline in a sensible order.
quests.explanation: Group emails should make the action easy to spot: everyone has to reply, so the deadline is placed in the closing sentence. The 'two more cars' shows the size of the problem.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are trying to find a date for a leaving party. Subject: Choosing a date for Hana's leaving party / Greeting: Hi all, / Arrange the body and sign-off.
options: Hana's last day is Friday, 27 June, and we would like to organise a small leaving party.
Please reply with your preference by Monday, and I will book the place.
The two options are lunch that day or drinks the evening before.

Cheers,
Luca
quests.hint: Context, then options, then deadline for the reply.
quests.explanation: Offering two options is easier to reply to than 'When are you free?'. The deadline tells everyone when the decision will be made.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are setting up a group project meeting and need everyone's availability. Subject: Meeting time for our presentation / Greeting: Hello team, / Arrange the message.
options:
Thanks,
Amira
We need to meet before the presentation on 20 March.
Could everybody tell me which of these times suits you by tomorrow evening?
I can do Monday after 3 pm, Tuesday morning, or Wednesday all day.
quests.hint: State the need, list what you can do, then ask everyone for a response.
quests.explanation: Listing your own options first makes replying easier. Setting a deadline for replies means you can fix the meeting without waiting indefinitely.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You have been offered a job but have accepted another one. Subject: Re: Offer of Data Analyst position / Greeting: Dear Ms Verma, / Arrange the body and sign-off.
options: I appreciated the time your team spent with me and wish you every success.

Yours sincerely,
Martin Keller
Thank you very much for offering me the Data Analyst position.
After careful thought, I have decided to accept another offer, so I must decline.
quests.hint: Thank them, decline clearly and end graciously.
quests.explanation: Employers remember polite refusals. Being clear in the second sentence prevents confusion, and a courteous ending keeps a professional door open.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You've been asked to join the school's parent committee but don't have the time. Subject: Re: Parent committee / Greeting: Dear Ms Sokolova, / Arrange the message.
options: I'd be glad to help with the summer fair, though, if a one-off task is useful.
Thank you for thinking of me for the parent committee.
I'm sorry, but I don't have enough time to give it the attention it deserves.

Kind regards,
Thomas Reid
quests.hint: Appreciate, decline, and offer something smaller.
quests.explanation: A refusal followed by a smaller offer shows goodwill. It also avoids the awkwardness of a flat 'no'.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A colleague asks you to work an extra shift, but you already have plans. Subject: Re: Extra shift on Sunday / Greeting: Hi Iris, / Arrange the reply.
options: I have a family event that I made plans for weeks ago.

Thanks,
Daniel
I'm afraid I can't cover Sunday's shift.
I hope you find someone, and I'm happy to take a shift next week if that helps.
quests.hint: A firm but friendly refusal has a clear 'no', a short reason and, if possible, an alternative.
quests.explanation: A short refusal is more honest than a vague reply. Including a reason makes it less personal, and an alternative shows you are still willing to help.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Your team-mate asked to swap sports kit numbers with you, but you prefer to keep yours. Subject: Re: Swapping numbers / Greeting: Hi Adam, / Arrange the friendly reply.
options: I hope that's okay, and I'm happy to help you pick a different one!
Thanks for asking about the kit numbers.

Cheers,
Niall
I'd rather keep number 7, because I've had it since the first season.
quests.hint: Tone is casual, but the refusal is still clear.
quests.explanation: Even among friends, a refusal works best when it is direct and kind. Explaining the sentimental value gives the reason without making Adam feel rejected.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You want to ask your manager to approve funding for a short training course. Subject: Request to attend the Excel training course / Greeting: Dear Mr Bianchi, / Arrange the body and sign-off.
options:
Kind regards,
Sandra Lopes
It would help me build the monthly reports faster, and I could share what I learn with the team.
I would like to ask for approval to attend the two-day Excel course on 9 and 10 July.
The fee is £340, and I have attached the course outline.
quests.hint: Request, benefit to the employer, then cost.
quests.explanation: A manager decides based on value. Benefit comes before cost, so the cost is read in context. The attachment keeps the message short.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You are contacting a tenant support helpline after a flood in your flat. Subject: Urgent: water leak in flat 6C / Greeting: Dear Housing Support, / Arrange the message.
options: Please call me on 07700 900123 to arrange an emergency visit.
I have turned off the water supply, but I need an engineer as soon as possible.

Yours faithfully,
Maya Singh
Water is leaking through the bathroom ceiling of flat 6C and has reached the hallway.
quests.hint: In an urgent email, the problem and the action come before background.
quests.explanation: In emergencies, the reader needs facts first: what is happening, what you already did, and how to reach you. Politeness remains, but there is no room for long explanations.
